events.name: The Diocese of Faroe is founded (approximate date)

events.enhanced_description: The invention of checkers, a strategy board game, reflects the growing interest in leisure activities and intellectual pursuits during the medieval period. The game has evolved over centuries, becoming a staple of board gaming worldwide.
events.name: Checkers is invented (approximate date)

events.enhanced_description: On February 23, 1100, Emperor Zhezong of the Song dynasty died after a 15-year reign, and was succeeded by his younger brother Huizong. During this period, the population of China reached around 100 million, with significant urban centers like Kaifeng thriving.
events.name: Emperor Zhezong dies

events.enhanced_description: In May or June 1100, Raymond IV of Saint-Gilles sailed to Constantinople seeking the support of Emperor Alexios I Komnenos for his campaign to seize Tripoli. This event highlights the alliances formed during the Crusades and the political maneuvers of the time.
events.name: Raymond IV sails to Constantinople

events.enhanced_description: In August 1100, during the Battle of Melitene, Bohemond I was captured by the Danishmends, leading to Tancred assuming the regency of the Principality of Antioch for two years. This battle was significant in the ongoing conflicts of the Crusades.
events.name: Battle of Melitene

events.enhanced_description: On August 2, 1100, King William II, also known as William Rufus, died in a hunting accident in the New Forest. Sir Walter Tirel was accused of the fatal shot but fled, leading to Henry I claiming the throne amidst political turmoil.
events.name: Death of King William II

events.enhanced_description: On August 5, 1100, Henry I was crowned King of England at Westminster Abbey. His ascension was marked by the necessity to appease the barons through the Charter of Liberties, an early example of a written constitution in Europe.
events.name: Henry I crowned King of England

events.enhanced_description: On August 20, 1100, Crusaders under Tancred, supported by a Venetian fleet, successfully captured the coastal city of Haifa. This victory was part of the broader Crusader efforts to secure key territories in the Levant.
events.name: Capture of Haifa

events.enhanced_description: On August 30, 1100, the Congress of Vytechev established peace and the feudal system in Kievan Rus, with the princes agreeing to share governance. Sviatopolk II of Kiev was recognized as the first Grand Prince, marking a significant political development.
events.name: Congress of Vytechev

events.enhanced_description: Antipope Clement III, who opposed the legitimate papacy during a tumultuous period of church politics, died after two decades of contention. His death marked a significant moment in the Investiture Controversy, as it allowed for the potential reconciliation of the factions within the Church.
events.name: Antipope Clement III dies at Civita Castellana after a 20-year reign in opposition to the legitimate popes Gregory VII, Victor III and Urban II

events.enhanced_description: On September 16, 1100, the Almoravid army defeated the Castellan troops at the Battle of Malagon. This battle was part of the larger conflict between the Almoravids and the Christian kingdoms in the Iberian Peninsula.
events.name: Battle of Malagon

events.enhanced_description: On September 23, 1100, Anselm, the Archbishop of Canterbury, returned from exile at the invitation of Henry I. His return was significant for the church's influence in England and the ongoing struggles between church and state.
events.name: Anselm returns from exile

events.enhanced_description: In September 1100, a Genoese fleet departed from Italy to assist the Crusaders in their efforts to conquer coastal cities, successfully reaching Latakia on September 25. This event underscores the maritime support that was crucial for the Crusader campaigns.
events.name: Genoese fleet reaches Latakia

events.enhanced_description: On October 18, 1100, Peter I of Aragon successfully conquered Barbastro from the Almoravids. This victory was part of the Reconquista, the Christian effort to reclaim territory in the Iberian Peninsula.
events.name: Peter I conquers Barbastro

events.enhanced_description: The council of Poitiers mandated that the followers of Robert of Arbrissel adopt a monastic lifestyle, which facilitated the establishment of Fontevraud Abbey. This abbey became a significant center for religious reform and women's monasticism in medieval France.
events.name: November – The council of Poitiers decrees that the followers of Robert of Arbrissel have to settle down and live under a rule, leading to the foundation of Fontevraud Abbey

events.enhanced_description: On November 11, 1100, Henry I married Matilda of Scotland, the daughter of King Malcolm III. This marriage strengthened ties between England and Scotland, reflecting the political alliances of the time.
events.name: Henry I marries Matilda of Scotland

events.enhanced_description: On November 18, 1100, the Council of Poitiers was convened but was forcibly closed by William IX, Duke of Aquitaine, as bishops were about to excommunicate King Philip I again. This event highlights the ongoing tensions between the monarchy and the church.
events.name: Council of Poitiers

events.enhanced_description: On December 25, 1100, Baldwin I was crowned the first King of Jerusalem at the Church of the Nativity in Bethlehem by Daimbert, the new Latin Patriarch. This event marked a significant moment in the establishment of Christian rule in the Holy Land following the Crusades.
events.name: Baldwin I crowned King of Jerusalem

events.enhanced_description: On December 25, 1100, King Philip I elevated his son Louis VI as co-ruler, marking a significant step in the transition of power within the French monarchy. This decision was aimed at solidifying the royal authority in the realm.
events.name: Philip I elevates Louis VI

events.enhanced_description: The Crusade of 1101 saw a renewed effort by European crusaders to reach the Holy Land, culminating in a disastrous defeat at the hands of the Seljuk Turks. Despite the setbacks, a small contingent managed to reach the Byzantine port of Bafra, illustrating the ongoing complexities of the Crusades.
events.name: Crusade of 1101 – A second wave of European crusaders attempts to cross Anatolia, to reach the Kingdom of Jerusalem

events.enhanced_description: The establishment of the county of Berg marked an important development in the feudal landscape of medieval Germany, contributing to the political fragmentation and local governance of the region. This new county would play a role in the evolving power dynamics of the Holy Roman Empire.
events.name: The county of Berg in Germany is established

events.enhanced_description: The completion of a comprehensive compilation of Buddhist writings from the Liao, Korean, and Song dynasties reflects the rich intellectual and spiritual traditions of East Asia during this period. This collection played a crucial role in the dissemination of Buddhist thought and practice across the region.
events.name: A vast compilation of Liao, Korean, and Song Buddhist writings is completed (approximate date)

events.enhanced_description: The founding of Fontevraud Abbey by Robert of Arbrissel marked a significant development in the history of monasticism in France, emphasizing a unique approach that included both men and women living under a common rule. The abbey became a center of religious reform and education in the medieval period.
events.name: Fontevraud Abbey is founded by the French preacher Robert of Arbrissel

events.enhanced_description: Ranulf Flambard's daring escape from the Tower of London to Normandy highlighted the political tensions of the time, as he sought refuge with Robert Curthose, a rival to the English throne. This event underscored the intricate relationships and conflicts among the nobility in early 12th-century England.
events.name: Ranulf Flambard, bishop of Durham, escapes from the Tower of London and flees to Normandy

events.enhanced_description: King Baldwin I's alliance with the Genoese fleet marked a significant diplomatic maneuver that enhanced the Crusader's military and economic strength in the region. This partnership facilitated the capture of key towns and solidified Baldwin's position in the Kingdom of Jerusalem.
events.name: Spring – King Baldwin I concludes an alliance with the Genoese fleet, offering them commercial privileges and booty

events.enhanced_description: The death of Antipope Theodoric marked a significant shift in the ongoing power struggle within the Church, as his supporters quickly rallied around Adalbert as his successor. This event underscored the contentious nature of papal authority and the influence of secular rulers in ecclesiastical matters.
events.name: Spring – Antipope Theodoric dies, the partisans of Emperor Henry IV choose Adalbert as the new antipope

events.enhanced_description: The canonization of King Canute IV as San Canuto reflected the growing veneration of saints in medieval Christianity and highlighted Canute's legacy as a ruler who promoted the Christian faith in Denmark. His sainthood contributed to the establishment of a national identity intertwined with religious devotion.
events.name: King Canute IV of Denmark is canonized as a saint under the name San Canuto

events.enhanced_description: The death of Roger I marked the end of a significant era in Sicilian history, as he had established the foundations of Norman rule in the region. His young son Simon succeeded him, with his mother acting as regent, indicating the continuation of Norman influence in southern Italy.
events.name: Roger I, count of Sicily, dies at Mileto in Calabria after a 30-year reign

events.enhanced_description: In a strategic military operation, Admiral Eustathios led the Byzantine fleet to reclaim key ports in western Cilicia from local powers. This victory not only reinforced Byzantine influence in the region but also showcased the naval capabilities of the Byzantine Empire during this period.
events.name: Summer – The Byzantine fleet under Admiral Eustathios recaptures the ports of western Cilicia, Seleucia and Corycus

events.enhanced_description: The siege of Valencia by Almoravid forces under Sultan Yusuf ibn Tashfin was a critical moment in the Reconquista, as it pitted Muslim forces against the defenders led by Jimena Díaz. The prolonged defense of the city exemplified the fierce resistance against Almoravid expansion in the Iberian Peninsula.
events.name: Summer – Almoravid forces under Sultan Yusuf ibn Tashfin besiege Valencia, which is defended by Jimena Díaz, widow of Rodrigo Diaz de Vivar

events.enhanced_description: Robert Curthose's landing at Portsmouth with an army marked a significant moment in the struggle for the English throne, as he sought to reclaim power from his brother Henry I. This conflict was part of the larger narrative of dynastic rivalry that characterized the period.
events.name: Robert Curthose lands at Portsmouth with an army in an effort to take the English throne from his younger brother, Henry I

events.enhanced_description: The Treaty of Alton was a pivotal agreement that resolved the immediate conflict between Robert Curthose and his brother Henry I, solidifying Henry's claim to the English throne. This treaty not only ended hostilities but also set the stage for future political dynamics in England.
events.name: By the Treaty of Alton, ratified at Winchester, Robert abandons his claim to the throne, recognising Henry as King of England

events.enhanced_description: The Battle of Ramla was a decisive confrontation where Baldwin I led a Crusader force to victory against the Fatimid army, showcasing the military prowess of the Crusaders. This victory allowed Baldwin to plunder the Fatimid camp and further consolidate Crusader control in the region.
events.name: Battle of Ramla: A Crusader force (some 1,100 men) under Baldwin I defeats the invading Fatimids at Ramla (modern Israel)

events.enhanced_description: Countess Mathilda of Tuscany's military expedition to Ferrara demonstrated her significant political and military influence in northern Italy. Her successful capture of the city reinforced her position as a powerful feudal lord during a time of fragmented political authority.
events.name: Autumn – Countess Mathilda of Tuscany leads a successful expedition in northern Italy and takes Ferrara

events.enhanced_description: The siege of Tripoli by Crusader forces under Raymond IV represented a strategic effort to expand Crusader control in the Levant. The siege was marked by military engagements with local defenders and highlighted the ongoing tensions between Christian and Muslim powers in the region.
events.name: Siege of Tripoli: The Crusaders under Raymond IV begin the siege of Tripoli (modern Lebanon)

events.enhanced_description: In early 1102, Raymond IV was imprisoned by Tancred, the regent of the Principality of Antioch and nephew of Bohemond I. He was later released after promising to renounce any claims to power, highlighting the political tensions within the Crusader states.
events.name: Raymond IV Imprisoned

events.enhanced_description: In 1102, Dagobert of Pisa was briefly deposed as Patriarch of Jerusalem, a significant religious position during the Crusades. He was restored later in the year, reflecting the turbulent nature of ecclesiastical authority in the region.
events.name: Dagobert of Pisa Deposed

events.enhanced_description: In 1102, the Venetians established a new trade emporium in Sidon, modern-day Lebanon, marking a significant expansion of their commercial influence in the Eastern Mediterranean. This development played a crucial role in the trade dynamics of the region.
events.name: Venetians Establish Trade Emporium

events.enhanced_description: In 1102, the Pacta Conventa was formed by the Croatian nobility, recognizing King Coloman as their overlord. This agreement initiated a personal union between the Kingdom of Hungary and Croatia, significantly impacting the political landscape of the region.
events.name: Pacta Conventa

events.enhanced_description: In 1102, King Henry I successfully captured Arundel Castle after besieging Earl Robert of Bellême. This victory resulted in the loss of Robert's English lands and his subsequent banishment to Normandy, altering the power dynamics in England.
events.name: Capture of Arundel Castle

events.enhanced_description: In 1102, King Henry I ordered the opening of Edward the Confessor's tomb, where the body was reportedly found undecayed. This event led to the monks of Westminster claiming Edward as a saint, enhancing his legacy within the church.
events.name: Opening of Edward the Confessor's Tomb

events.enhanced_description: The invasion of Palestine by a large Fatimid force marked a critical moment in the ongoing conflicts of the Crusades, as they launched significant attacks against Crusader-held territories. This military campaign underscored the volatility of the region and the continuing struggle for control over the Holy Land.
events.name: Spring – A Fatimid expeditionary force (some 20,000 men) invades Palestine and launches attacks into the Kingdom of Jerusalem

events.enhanced_description: On May 5, 1102, Valencia fell to Almoravid forces under Sultan Yusuf ibn Tashfin, marking the end of the principality established by Rodrigo Diaz de Vivar, known as El Cid. The city would later be recaptured and destroyed by King Alfonso VI.
events.name: Fall of Valencia

events.enhanced_description: On May 27, 1102, the Crusaders under King Baldwin I executed a daring breakout from Jaffa, which was besieged by the Fatimid army. A cavalry charge by the French forces broke the enemy's ranks, leading to a retreat towards Ascalon.
events.name: Crusaders Break Out of Jaffa

events.enhanced_description: Władysław I Herman, the Duke of Poland, died on June 4, 1102, in Płock, possibly poisoned by his enemies. His death led to a succession dispute between his sons Zbigniew and Bolesław III Wrymouth, which would shape Polish politics for years to come.
events.name: Death of Władysław I Herman

events.enhanced_description: In 1103, the Crusaders under Raymond IV invaded the Beqaa Valley and captured Tortosa, effectively isolating Tripoli. This strategic move was supported by a Byzantine fleet, marking a significant military achievement in the ongoing Crusades.
events.name: Crusaders Capture Tortosa

events.enhanced_description: In 1103, Li Jie, a Chinese government minister, published his influential technical treatise, Yingzao Fashi, on architecture during the reign of Emperor Hui Zong of the Song Dynasty. This work became a foundational text in Chinese architectural practice.
events.name: Li Jie's Yingzao Fashi Publication

events.enhanced_description: Around 1103, the city of Lund in the Swedish province of Scania was established as a see of the Catholic Church, becoming the Archdiocese of Lund. This development marked a significant moment in the spread of Christianity in Scandinavia.
events.name: Archdiocese of Lund Established

events.enhanced_description: In the spring of 1103, Bohemond I, the Norman prince of Antioch, was released from Seljuk imprisonment in Niksar after a hefty ransom was paid. His return shifted the power dynamics in the region, as Tancred had been expanding territorial control during Bohemond's absence.
events.name: Release of Bohemond I

events.enhanced_description: On April 27, 1103, Anselm, Archbishop of Canterbury, went into exile again following a dispute with King Henry I regarding the appointment of bishops and abbots. This conflict underscored the ongoing tensions between church and state during this period.
events.name: Anselm's Exile

events.enhanced_description: During the summer of 1103, Crusaders led by Bohemond I and Joscelin of Courtenay raided the territory of Aleppo to secure supplies. They successfully captured the town of Muslimiyah and negotiated a tribute from the Seljuk ruler, showcasing their military prowess.
events.name: Crusaders Raid Aleppo

events.enhanced_description: On August 5, 1103, Matilda of Scotland, wife of King Henry I, gave birth to their first son, William Adelin, in Winchester. This event was significant for the royal lineage and the future of the English monarchy.
events.name: Birth of William Adelin

events.enhanced_description: On August 24, 1103, King Magnus III of Norway was killed in battle against the Ulaid in Ulster. His death led to a power-sharing arrangement among his sons, Sigurd Jorsalfare, Øystein Magnusson, and Olaf Magnusson, as they became joint kings of Norway.
events.name: Death of King Magnus III

events.enhanced_description: In 1104, Toghtekin, the Seljuk ruler of Damascus, founded a short-lived principality in Syria, marking the beginning of a series of Seljuk-ruled dynasties in the region. This development was significant in the context of the ongoing power struggles in the Middle East.
events.name: Toghtekin Founding Principality

events.enhanced_description: In a remarkable military feat, King David IV of Georgia led a small force of approximately 1,500 men to defeat a vastly larger army of 100,000 Seljuk Turks. This victory was pivotal in establishing Georgian independence and strength in the region.
events.name: King David IV of Georgia defeats Seljuk Turks

events.enhanced_description: Sultan Kilij Arslan I of the Sultanate of Rum initiated hostilities against the Danishmendids, marking a significant conflict in the power struggles of the region during the Crusades. This war would have lasting implications for control over Anatolia.
events.name: Sultan Kilij Arslan I starts a war with the Danishmendids

events.enhanced_description: The establishment of the Venetian Arsenal in Venice marked a critical development in naval warfare and shipbuilding technology. This facility would become a cornerstone of Venice's maritime power and economic strength in the Mediterranean.
events.name: The Venetian Arsenal is founded in Venice

events.enhanced_description: In the spring of 1104, the Crusaders, led by Bohemond I, attempted to re-invade the territory of Aleppo and capture the town of Kafar Latha. However, the attack failed due to strong resistance from the local Banu tribe.
events.name: Crusaders Re-invade Aleppo

events.enhanced_description: The dedication of the new basilica at Vézelay Abbey was a significant event in the religious landscape of medieval France, symbolizing the importance of pilgrimage and monastic life. The abbey became a key site for the promotion of the Crusades.
events.name: The new basilica at Vézelay Abbey is dedicated

events.enhanced_description: On May 7, 1104, the Crusaders under Baldwin II faced a devastating defeat at the Battle of Harran against the Seljuk Turks. Both Baldwin and Joscelin of Courtenay were captured, leading to Tancred becoming the regent of Edessa and marking a turning point in Crusader expansion.
events.name: Battle of Harran

events.enhanced_description: On May 26, 1104, King Baldwin I captured Acre after a prolonged siege that began in April. The port city was blockaded by Genoese and Pisan fleets, and Baldwin's victory was marred by the plundering of Muslim emigrants by Italian sailors.
events.name: Capture of Acre

events.enhanced_description: In the summer of 1104, the Byzantines re-occupied the Cilician cities of Tarsus, Adana, and Mamistra, marking a significant military achievement. A naval squadron led by Admiral Cantacuzenus played a crucial role in this campaign, enhancing Byzantine influence in the region.
events.name: Byzantines Re-occupy Cilician Cities

events.enhanced_description: The reburial of St. Cuthbert in Durham Cathedral marked a significant moment in the history of Christianity in England, symbolizing the importance of saints in medieval religious life. This event solidified Durham's status as a center of pilgrimage and devotion.
events.name: St. Cuthbert is reburied in Durham Cathedral

events.enhanced_description: Following the death of his half-brother Peter I, Alfonso I ascended to the throne of Aragon and Navarre, unifying the two regions under his rule. His reign would be marked by efforts to expand Christian territories in the Iberian Peninsula.
events.name: Alfonso I becomes king of Aragon and Navarre

events.enhanced_description: In the autumn of 1104, Bohemond I departed for Italy to gather reinforcements for his campaigns. His absence allowed Tancred to assume co-rulership over Antioch, indicating the shifting power dynamics within the Crusader states.
events.name: Bohemond I Departs for Reinforcements

events.enhanced_description: The eruption of Hekla in Iceland during the autumn of 1104 had devastating effects on the surrounding agricultural lands, affecting the livelihoods of local communities. This natural disaster is one of the many significant volcanic events in Iceland's history.
events.name: Hekla erupts in Iceland

events.enhanced_description: Almoravid emir Yusuf ibn Tashfin dispatched a fleet to Palestine to counter the Crusader presence, but the expedition was tragically lost at sea. This event highlights the challenges faced by Muslim leaders in responding to Crusader advances.
events.name: Yusuf ibn Tashfin sends maritime expedition to Palestine

events.enhanced_description: Bohemond I's return to Apulia after nine years marked a significant moment in the political landscape of Southern Italy, as he sought to consolidate power and strengthen ties with the papacy. His meeting with Pope Paschal II underscored the importance of ecclesiastical support.
events.name: Bohemond I arrives in Apulia

events.enhanced_description: During their visit to King Philip I's court, Bohemond I and papal legate Bruno sought to recruit men for their military campaigns, reflecting the ongoing alliances and political maneuvering of the Crusader states.
events.name: Bohemond I and Bruno visit King Philip I

events.enhanced_description: The death of Inge the Elder led to a succession crisis in Sweden, with his nephew Philip taking the throne alongside his brother. This transition marked a significant moment in the governance of Sweden during the early 12th century.
events.name: Inge the Elder dies

events.enhanced_description: The meeting between Henry I and Anselm, archbishop of Canterbury, was crucial in resolving their disputes that had led to Anselm's exile. This encounter underscored the tension between church and state during this period.
events.name: Henry I meets Anselm

events.enhanced_description: The death of Sultan Barkiyaruq marked a significant shift in the Seljuk Empire's leadership, leading to a power struggle between his son Malik-Shah II and his uncle Muhammad I. This transition would affect the stability of the empire in the years to come.
events.name: Sultan Barkiyaruq dies

events.enhanced_description: The annexation of the Tamna Kingdom by the Goryeo Dynasty marked a significant expansion of Goryeo's territorial influence in Korea. This event reflects the consolidation of power and the unification efforts of the Goryeo rulers.
events.name: Tamna Kingdom is annexed by Goryeo Dynasty

events.enhanced_description: The election of Sylvester IV as antipope in Rome, supported by Henry V, highlighted the ongoing conflicts within the Church and the political machinations of the time. This event underscored the complexities of papal authority during the Investiture Controversy.
events.name: Sylvester IV is elected as antipope

events.enhanced_description: The death of Raymond IV at his castle of Mons Peregrinus marked a pivotal transition in the leadership of the County of Tripoli. His young son Alfonso I was left to rule, with his nephew William-Jordan appointed as regent, shaping the future of the region.
events.name: Raymond IV dies at Mons Peregrinus

events.enhanced_description: In the Battle of Artah, Crusaders led by Tancred achieved a decisive victory against a Seljuk army, significantly enhancing their control over the region. This battle was part of the broader Crusader efforts to expand their territories in the Levant.
events.name: Battle of Artah

events.enhanced_description: Henry I's invasion of Normandy was a strategic military campaign aimed at reclaiming territory from his brother Robert II. The successful capture of Bayeux and Caen showcased Henry's military prowess, although subsequent negotiations remained inconclusive.
events.name: Henry I invades Normandy

events.enhanced_description: The Battle of Ramla, fought on May 17, 1102, saw the Crusaders, led by King Baldwin I, suffer a significant defeat against the Fatimid army. Despite the loss, Baldwin and his knights managed to escape through enemy lines to Arsuf, showcasing their resilience amidst adversity.
events.name: Battle of Ramla

events.enhanced_description: Sultan Kilij Arslan I's expedition to Melitene represented a strategic attempt to expand Seljuk influence in the region. Despite initial successes, the strong defenses of Edessa thwarted his ambitions, highlighting the challenges faced by the Seljuks against Crusader fortifications.
events.name: Kilij Arslan I leads Seljuk expedition to Melitene

events.enhanced_description: The deposition of Henry IV by his son Henry V marked a significant turning point in the power dynamics of the Holy Roman Empire, leading to a period of political instability and conflict between the two rulers.
events.name: Henry IV is deposed by Henry V

events.enhanced_description: Sultan Yusuf ibn Tashfin, the founder of the Almoravid Empire, dies after a lengthy reign of 45 years. His death leads to the ascension of his young son, Ali ibn Yusuf, who appoints his brother Tamin as governor of Al-Andalus, marking a significant transition in leadership for the empire.
events.name: Sultan Yusuf ibn Tashfin dies after a 45-year reign

events.enhanced_description: Duke Bolesław III of Poland initiates a civil war against his half-brother Zbigniew, seeking control over the regions of Lesser Poland and Silesia. This conflict marks a significant power struggle within the Polish nobility, impacting the political landscape of the region.
events.name: Bolesław III, duke of Poland, begins a civil war against his half-brother Zbigniew

events.enhanced_description: Ermengol VI, the count of Urgell, successfully conquers the city of Balaguer from Moorish control. This victory is part of the broader Christian Reconquista efforts in the Iberian Peninsula during the 11th century.
events.name: The city of Balaguer is conquered from the Moors by Ermengol VI

events.enhanced_description: Roger le Poer, the bishop of Salisbury, receives land in south Wales from King Henry I, leading to the construction of Kidwelly Castle on the banks of the river Gwendraeth. This event highlights the intertwining of ecclesiastical authority and feudal power in medieval Britain.
events.name: Roger le Poer is granted land in south Wales by Henry I

events.enhanced_description: Magnus Erlendsson is appointed as Earl of Orkney, a title he will hold until 1115. His leadership is significant for the governance and development of the Orkney Islands during this period.
events.name: Magnus Erlendsson becomes Earl of Orkney

events.enhanced_description: The Great Comet of 1106 is observed by various civilizations around the world, captivating observers with its brightness over a period of 40 days. This astronomical event is noted in historical records, reflecting the human fascination with celestial phenomena.
events.name: The Great Comet of 1106 is seen

events.enhanced_description: The marriage of Bohemond I to Constance of France in Chartres Cathedral was a significant political alliance that strengthened ties between the Crusader states and the French monarchy. This union also facilitated Bohemond's military ambitions against the Byzantine Empire.
events.name: Bohemond I marries Constance of France

events.enhanced_description: Emperor Henry IV's daring escape from captivity at Ingelheim allowed him to regroup and negotiate with various noble factions, demonstrating the ongoing political turmoil within the Holy Roman Empire. His subsequent actions would shape the future of the empire.
events.name: Henry IV escapes his captors

events.enhanced_description: In the Battle of Tinchebray, King Henry I defeated and captured his brother Robert II, solidifying his control over Normandy. This victory not only secured Henry's power but also had lasting implications for the English and Norman realms.
events.name: Battle of Tinchebray

events.enhanced_description: Bohemond I's return to Apulia with an expeditionary force was a strategic move to prepare for an offensive against the Byzantines. Accompanied by his pregnant wife Constance, this event marked a significant moment in the ongoing conflicts between Crusaders and the Byzantine Empire.
events.name: Bohemond I returns to Apulia

events.enhanced_description: In the spring, Duke Bolesław III of Poland, alongside his ally King Coloman of Hungary, invades Bohemia to support Duke Svatopluk's claim to the throne. Their successful campaign culminates in Svatopluk's installation as Duke of Bohemia, showcasing the shifting alliances and power dynamics of the region.
events.name: Duke Bolesław III invades Bohemia

events.enhanced_description: In the autumn, King Sigurd I of Norway embarks on a crusade to the Holy Land, leading a fleet of 60 ships and approximately 5,000 men. His journey marks a significant moment in the Norwegian Crusade, as he becomes the first European king to actively support the Crusaders in the Levant.
events.name: King Sigurd I sails for the Holy Land

events.enhanced_description: In November, Bohemond I initiates the siege of Dyrrhachium, an important Adriatic port city held by the Byzantine doux Alexios Komnenos. This siege reflects the ongoing tensions and military engagements between the Crusader states and the Byzantine Empire.
events.name: Siege of Dyrrhachium begins

events.enhanced_description: During the winter, Bolesław III launches a punitive expedition against his half-brother Zbigniew, enlisting the support of Kievan and Hungarian allies. This conflict illustrates the intense familial and political rivalries that characterized the Polish nobility during this period.
events.name: Bolesław III's punitive expedition

events.enhanced_description: Saracen pirates conduct a raid on the Benedictine monastery of Saint Honorat, located on the Lérins Islands. This event underscores the ongoing maritime threats faced by Christian territories in the Mediterranean during the medieval period.
events.name: Saracen pirates raid the monastery of Saint Honorat

events.enhanced_description: In June, Kilij Arslan I, the sultan of the Sultanate of Rum, conquers Mosul during the Battle of Mosul. However, he faces a significant defeat and is ultimately killed by Seljuk forces, marking a pivotal moment in the power struggles of the region.
events.name: Kilij Arslan I conquers Mosul

events.enhanced_description: The Crusaders, led by Tancred, prince of Galilee, successfully recover the Cilician cities of Tarsus, Adana, and Mamistra, which had been conquered by Emperor Alexios I three years prior. This recovery is a significant achievement for the Crusaders in the region.
events.name: Crusaders recover Cilician cities

events.enhanced_description: Joscelin I, lord of Turbessel, is released from captivity by Ilghazi, the Artukid ruler of Mardin, after paying a ransom of 20,000 dinars and promising military aid. This event highlights the complex political dynamics and alliances in the region during this period.
events.name: Joscelin I is released by Ilghazi

events.enhanced_description: Emir Fadl ibn Rabi'ah is expelled from Damascus by Toghtekin, the atabeg of the city. This event reflects the shifting power dynamics in the region as local rulers vie for control.
events.name: Emir Fadl ibn Rabi'ah is expelled by Toghtekin

events.enhanced_description: In an effort to combat counterfeiting, Chinese authorities begin printing paper money in three colors. This innovation represents a significant development in the economic practices of the Song Dynasty.
events.name: Chinese authorities print paper money

events.enhanced_description: Emperor Hui Zong of China authors the 'Treatise on Tea,' providing the most detailed account of the sophisticated tea ceremony practiced during the Song Dynasty. This work highlights the cultural significance of tea in Chinese society.
events.name: Emperor Hui Zong writes his Treatise on Tea

events.enhanced_description: King Edgar of Scotland dies at Edinburgh Castle after a nine-year reign, leading to the succession of his brother Alexander I. This transition of power is marked by internal divisions, as David I becomes co-ruler in Lothian and Strathclyde, indicating emerging tensions within the royal family.
events.name: King Edgar dies at Edinburgh Castle

events.enhanced_description: Emperor Horikawa of Japan dies after a 20-year reign, and his 4-year-old son Toba ascends to the throne. This transition marks a significant moment in Japanese history, as the young emperor's reign will be influenced by regents and court factions.
events.name: Emperor Horikawa dies and is succeeded by Toba

events.enhanced_description: The Investiture Controversy reaches a resolution with the reconciliation of King Henry I and Anselm, the archbishop of Canterbury. This pivotal moment is marked by the mass consecration of bishops, reinforcing the relationship between the monarchy and the church in medieval England.
events.name: The Investiture Controversy is resolved

events.enhanced_description: Bohemond I, prince of Antioch, lands with a substantial army in Epirus, near Avlona, where he begins to plunder the countryside. This military action is part of the broader conflicts involving the Crusader states and the Byzantine Empire.
events.name: Bohemond I lands in Epirus

events.enhanced_description: In the spring, King Sigurd I of Norway sets sail from England on his crusade to Palestine. His journey includes repelling a Muslim fleet near the Tagus River and attacking key locations in the Iberian Peninsula, showcasing his military ambitions in support of the Crusader cause.
events.name: King Sigurd I sails from England

events.enhanced_description: In September, Bohemond I's forces lift the siege of Dyrrhachium due to illness and supply shortages. Following this, Bohemond becomes a vassal of the Byzantine Empire by signing the Treaty of Devol, marking a significant shift in allegiances.
events.name: Siege of Dyrrhachium lifted

events.enhanced_description: In 1108, the first mention of consuls in Bergamo signifies the city's transition to an independent commune, reflecting the growing trend of self-governance in Northern Italy during the medieval period. This development was part of a broader movement towards civic autonomy in Italian city-states.
events.name: The consuls of Bergamo are first mentioned, indicating that the city has become an independent commune in Lombardy (Northern Italy)

events.enhanced_description: In 1108, Baldwin I of Jerusalem led an expedition against Sidon, supported by a fleet of sailor-adventurers from various Italian cities. This military action culminated in a naval battle where a Fatimid fleet defeated the Italians, showcasing the ongoing conflict between Crusader states and Muslim powers in the region.
events.name: Baldwin I marches out against Sidon, with the support of a squadron of sailor-adventurers from various Italian cities

events.enhanced_description: In 1108, the Taira and Minamoto clans united to establish their dominance over Japan following a decisive victory against the warrior monks of the Enryaku-ji temple. This alliance marked a pivotal moment in Japanese history, leading to the eventual rise of samurai rule.
events.name: The Taira and Minamoto clans join forces to rule Japan, after defeating the warrior monks of the Enryaku-ji temple near Kyoto

events.enhanced_description: In 1108, Chichester Cathedral was consecrated by Bishop Ralph de Luffa, marking a significant event in the religious and architectural history of England. This cathedral became a central place of worship and a symbol of the growing influence of the Church in medieval society.
events.name: Chichester Cathedral is consecrated under Ralph de Luffa, bishop of Chichester, in England

events.enhanced_description: The construction of the tower of Winchester Cathedral commenced in 1108, representing a significant architectural endeavor that would continue until 1120. This project not only showcased the skill of medieval builders but also reflected the importance of cathedrals as centers of community and faith.
events.name: Construction begins on the tower of Winchester Cathedral, building continues until 1120

events.enhanced_description: In 1108, Pistoia Cathedral suffered significant damage due to a severe fire, impacting the local community and its religious practices. The incident highlighted the vulnerabilities of medieval structures and the challenges faced by towns in preserving their cultural heritage.
events.name: Pistoia Cathedral in Italy is damaged by a severe fire

events.enhanced_description: The Battle of Uclés sees Almoravid forces decisively defeat the armies of Castile and León, halting the advance of the Reconquista. The battle results in the recapture of several towns and a significant loss of life among the Christian nobility.
events.name: Battle of Uclés

events.enhanced_description: On June 13, 1108, the restored Ferentino Cathedral in Italy was consecrated, marking its return as a vital place of worship and community gathering. This event underscored the importance of cathedrals in medieval society as centers of faith and culture.
events.name: – Restored Ferentino Cathedral in Italy is consecrated

events.enhanced_description: In the summer of 1108, Jawali Saqawa, the Turkish ruler of Mosul, accepted a substantial ransom of 30,000 dinars from Count Joscelin I for the release of Baldwin II, the count of Edessa, who had been captured. This event illustrates the complex political dynamics and the high stakes of power during the Crusades.
events.name: Summer – Jawali Saqawa, Turkish ruler of Mosul, accepts a ransom of 30,000 dinar by Count Joscelin I and releases his cousin Baldwin II, count of Edessa, who is held as prisoner (see 1104)

events.enhanced_description: King Philip I of France dies in Melun after a 48-year reign, leading to the succession of his son Louis VI. The new king faces immediate challenges from rebellious feudal lords, setting the stage for a tumultuous reign.
events.name: King Philip I dies at Melun

events.enhanced_description: In the autumn of 1108, King Coloman of Hungary effectively ended the existence of the Principality of Nitra by deposing its last ruler, Álmos, who was also the duke of Croatia. This event marked a significant consolidation of power for Hungary in the region.
events.name: Autumn – The Principality of Nitra ceases to exist, after King Coloman of Hungary, deposes its last ruler, Álmos, duke of Croatia

events.enhanced_description: In 1109, the Almoravid army, commanded by Ali ibn Yusuf, attempted to recapture Toledo, which had been lost in 1085. The failure of this campaign highlighted the ongoing struggles between Muslim and Christian forces in the Iberian Peninsula during the Reconquista.
events.name: The Almoravid army, led by Ali ibn Yusuf, fails to reconquer Toledo (lost in 1085)

events.enhanced_description: In 1109, Bolesław III achieved a significant victory against the imperial forces led by Henry V at the Battle of Hundsfeld. This ambush demonstrated the effectiveness of Polish military tactics and solidified Bolesław's position in the region.
events.name: Battle of Hundsfeld: Bolesław III defeats the imperial forces under Henry V at Hundsfeld

events.enhanced_description: Around 1109, Anselm of Laon, a prominent French monk and theologian, was appointed chancellor of the cathedral at Laon. His role was significant in the intellectual and religious life of the time, contributing to the development of scholastic thought.
events.name: Anselm of Laon, French monk and theologian, becomes chancellor of the cathedral at Laon (approximate date)

events.enhanced_description: In the summer of 1109, Almoravid emir Ali ibn Yusuf orchestrated a public ritual of penance in Cordoba, burning the works of the influential philosopher Al-Ghazali. This act reflected the tensions between different philosophical and theological schools within Islamic thought during this period.
events.name: Summer – Almoravid emir Ali ibn Yusuf organizes a public ritual of penance (auto-da-fé) of the works of Al-Ghazali, in front of the Great Mosque of Cordoba

events.enhanced_description: On July 1, 1109, Urraca of León ascended to the throne as queen of León, Castile, and Galicia following the death of her father, King Alfonso VI. This historic event marked her as the first queen regnant in Europe, paving the way for female leadership in medieval politics.
events.name: – Urraca of León becomes queen of León, Castile and Galicia after the death of her father, King Alfonso VI, making her the first European queen regnant

events.enhanced_description: On July 12, 1109, after a prolonged seven-year siege, Tripoli fell to the Crusaders, supported by the Genoese fleet. This victory established the County of Tripoli as the fourth Crusader state in the Middle East, significantly altering the power dynamics in the region.
events.name: – Siege of Tripoli: After a 7-year siege (supported by the Genoese fleet), Tripoli falls to the Crusaders

events.enhanced_description: On August 10, 1109, Bolesław III led a military expedition into Pomerania, where he besieged the castle of Nakło and successfully defeated a Pomeranian relief force. This battle was part of Bolesław's efforts to expand Polish territory and influence in the region.
events.name: – Battle of Nakło: Bolesław III leads an expedition into Pomerania

events.enhanced_description: On August 24, 1109, German forces under King Henry V laid siege to Głogów but were ultimately forced to abandon the effort due to fierce resistance from Polish guerrilla warriors. This event underscored the challenges faced by the German monarchy in expanding its influence in Eastern Europe.
events.name: Siege of Głogów: German forces led by King Henry V besiege Głogów

events.enhanced_description: In 1110, the Second Chola invasion of Kalinga marked a significant military campaign aimed at expanding Chola influence in the region. This invasion was part of the Chola dynasty's broader efforts to assert control over southern India and beyond.
events.name: Second Chola invasion of Kalinga

events.enhanced_description: In 1110, Henry V, King of Germany, invaded Italy with a significant military force and reached an agreement with Pope Paschal II at Sutri. This accord involved Henry renouncing the contentious right of investiture, marking a crucial moment in the Investiture Controversy and the relationship between the monarchy and the papacy.
events.name: Henry V, King of Germany, invades Italy with a large army and concludes an agreement with Pope Paschal II at Sutri

events.enhanced_description: Following the assassination of Svatopluk, known as 'the Lion', Vladislaus I secures the dukedom of Bohemia with the backing of Henry V. His rule marks a significant period in Bohemian history, lasting until 1125.
events.name: The dukedom of Bohemia is secured for Vladislaus I following the death of Svatopluk ("the Lion") who is assassinated

events.enhanced_description: Sultan Ali ibn Yusuf leads Almoravid forces to occupy Zaragoza, consolidating control over all Muslim states in Andalusia. This occupation signifies a pivotal moment in the Almoravid expansion in the Iberian Peninsula.
events.name: Almoravid forces under Sultan Ali ibn Yusuf occupy Zaragoza (modern Spain)

events.enhanced_description: King Henry I commissions significant improvements at Windsor Castle, including the construction of a chapel, transforming it into his formal residence. This development reflects the growing importance of royal residences in medieval England.
events.name: King Henry I has improvements made at Windsor Castle

events.enhanced_description: The completion of the Rus' Primary Chronicle marks a crucial moment in the documentation of East Slavic history. This chronicle serves as a foundational text for understanding the early history and culture of the Kievan Rus.
events.name: The Rus' Primary Chronicle is completed

events.enhanced_description: The Kalingattuparani, a Tamil epic by Jayamkondar, is composed around this time, celebrating the victory of Kulottunga Chola I over the Kalinga king Anantavarman Chodaganga. This work is significant in Tamil literature and cultural identity.
events.name: Approximate date of composition of Jayamkondar's Kalingattuparani

events.enhanced_description: The construction of Fontevraud Abbey begins in Anjou, which will become a significant religious and cultural site in France. This abbey is notable for its unique blend of monastic traditions and architectural styles.
events.name: Construction begins on Fontevraud Abbey in the French duchy of Anjou

events.enhanced_description: From February to May 1110, Crusaders led by Baldwin I besieged the city of Beirut, employing a blockade with Genoese and Pisan ships. The siege culminated in the capture of the city on May 13, marking a significant victory for the Crusaders in their campaign to expand their territories.
events.name: February–May – Crusaders under Baldwin I besiege Beirut

events.enhanced_description: In the spring of 1110, Mawdud ibn Altuntash, the Turkic atabeg of Mosul, launched an expedition to seize Crusader territories east of the Euphrates River, specifically targeting the County of Edessa. However, he was forced to retreat when Baldwin I of Jerusalem intervened with a relief force, highlighting the ongoing conflicts during the Crusades.
events.name: Spring – Mawdud ibn Altuntash, Turkic ruler (atabeg) of Mosul, leads an expedition to capture the territories of the Crusaders (belonging to the County of Edessa) east of the river Euphrates

events.enhanced_description: On May 5, 1110, a lunar eclipse occurred, during which the moon became completely dark, as recorded by the Peterborough Chronicle. This phenomenon was attributed to aerosols from a previous volcanic eruption, illustrating the interplay between natural events and human observation in medieval times.
events.name: Lunar eclipse, in which the moon becomes totally dark (according to the Peterborough Chronicle), due to an earlier volcanic eruption putting aerosols into the upper atmosphere of the earth, thus cutting off the earthlight

events.enhanced_description: In a politically motivated union, Henry V marries the young Matilda, the daughter of King Henry I of England, in Mainz. This marriage is significant as it aims to strengthen ties between the Holy Roman Empire and England, while Matilda is placed under the care of Archbishop Bruno for her education in German culture.
events.name: Henry V marries 8-year-old Matilda (daughter of King Henry I of England)

events.enhanced_description: Between October and December 1110, Crusaders under Baldwin I, with support from King Sigurd I of Norway, besieged Sidon. Despite challenges from a powerful Fatimid flotilla, the siege ended successfully on December 4, when the city capitulated, further solidifying Crusader control in the region.
events.name: October–December – Crusaders under Baldwin I (supported by King Sigurd I) besiege Sidon

events.enhanced_description: In December 1110, Tancred, the Italo-Norman prince of Galilee, successfully took control of the Crusader castle Krak des Chevaliers in Syria. This strategic stronghold became a key point of defense and influence for the Crusaders in the region.
events.name: December – Tancred, Italo-Norman prince of Galilee, brings the Crusader castle Krak des Chevaliers in Syria under his control

events.enhanced_description: In the Battle of Shaizar, Sultan Muhammad I Tapar appoints Mawdud ibn Altuntash to lead a Seljuk expedition against the Crusaders, resulting in significant losses for King Baldwin I of Jerusalem's forces. This battle highlights the ongoing conflicts between Crusaders and Muslim powers in the region.
events.name: Battle of Shaizar

events.enhanced_description: During the winter, Crusaders led by Baldwin I lay siege to Tyre without naval support, facing challenges from both the city and external forces. The siege reflects the ongoing struggles of the Crusaders to maintain their foothold in the Holy Land.
events.name: Winter – Crusaders, led by Baldwin I, besiege Tyre

events.enhanced_description: Almoravid forces, led by Syr ibn Abi Bakr, capture the towns of Santarém and Sintra, furthering their campaign in the Iberian Peninsula. This military action is part of a broader effort to reclaim territories lost to Christian forces.
events.name: Almoravid forces under Syr ibn Abi Bakr capture Santarém and Sintra

events.enhanced_description: Milanese troops besiege and ultimately destroy the commune of Lodi Vecchio, marking a significant event in the power struggles of northern Italy. This destruction reflects the intense rivalries among Italian city-states during this period.
events.name: The commune of Lodi Vecchio is besieged and destroyed by Milanese troops

events.enhanced_description: Domnall Gerrlámhach is appointed king of the Hebrides and the Isle of Man, following a request from the people of Munster for a ruler. His ascension signifies the interconnectedness of Irish and Scottish leadership during this era.
events.name: Domnall Gerrlámhach becomes king of the Hebrides and the Isle of Man

events.enhanced_description: The establishment of the Donglin Academy in Wuxi marks a significant development in Chinese education during the Northern Song dynasty. This institution becomes a center for Confucian learning and scholarship.
events.name: The Donglin Academy is established in Wuxi during the Northern Song dynasty

events.enhanced_description: The Synod of Rathbreasail represents a pivotal moment in the Irish church, transitioning from a monastic to a diocesan structure. This change reflects broader trends in ecclesiastical organization across Europe.
events.name: The Synod of Rathbreasail marks the transition of the Irish church

events.enhanced_description: In a decisive encounter at the Salnitsa river, Prince Vladimir of Kievan Rus' delivers a crushing defeat to the Cumans, solidifying his power and influence in the region. This victory is pivotal in the ongoing conflicts between the Kievan Rus and nomadic tribes.
events.name: Battle of the Salnitsa river

events.enhanced_description: Henry V is crowned Holy Roman Emperor by Pope Paschal II, marking a significant moment in the relationship between the papacy and the Holy Roman Empire. Following his coronation, Henry strengthens his influence by granting privileges to German nobles.
events.name: Henry V is crowned as Holy Roman Emperor by Pope Paschal II

events.enhanced_description: At the age of 18, Baldwin VII ascends to the title of Count of Flanders following the death of his father, Robert II. His reign will last until 1119, shaping the political landscape of the region.
events.name: 18-year-old Baldwin VII succeeds his father, Robert II, as Count of Flanders

events.enhanced_description: Duke Bolesław III Wrymouth commits a brutal act by blinding his half-brother Zbigniew and imprisoning him in Tyniec Abbey, leading to his excommunication by Archbishop Martin I. This incident reflects the violent power struggles within Polish nobility.
events.name: Duke Bolesław III Wrymouth blinds his half-brother Zbigniew

events.enhanced_description: Otto, known as 'the Rich', is appointed duke of Saxony by Emperor Henry V, although he will later be stripped of this title. This appointment illustrates the shifting allegiances and power dynamics within the Holy Roman Empire.
events.name: Otto is appointed duke of Saxony by Emperor Henry V

events.enhanced_description: The founding of Salzwedel in the Altmark marks the establishment of a new settlement in Germany during this period. This development reflects the broader trends of urbanization and settlement expansion in medieval Europe.
events.name: Salzwedel in the Altmark is founded

events.enhanced_description: The Margraviate of Baden was established by Herman II, marking a significant political development in the region. This foundation laid the groundwork for the future Duchy of Baden, which would play a crucial role in the political landscape of Germany.
events.name: The Margraviate of Baden is founded by Herman II

events.enhanced_description: Gallus Anonymus, a notable Polish chronicler, began composing 'Gesta principum Polonorum,' a foundational historical text that documented the early Polish princes and their deeds. This work is essential for understanding the history and development of Poland during the medieval period.
events.name: Gallus Anonymus, Polish chronicler and historian, begins to write Gesta principum Polonorum, to Bolesław III

events.enhanced_description: During Easter, the citizens of Laon declared a commune and violently executed Bishop Waldric in his cathedral, reflecting the rising tensions between local governance and ecclesiastical authority. This event marked a significant moment in the struggle for civic rights in medieval France.
events.name: Easter – The citizens of Laon in France, having proclaimed a commune, murder Bishop Waldric in his cathedral

events.enhanced_description: Through his marriage to Douce I, the heiress of Provence, Ramon Berenguer III expands his dominion, significantly enhancing his power in the region. This union illustrates the importance of marriage alliances in medieval politics.
events.name: Ramon Berenguer III obtains the county of Provence

events.enhanced_description: In the spring, Malik Shah, the Seljuk ruler of the Sultanate of Rum, initiates military incursions into Anatolia, aiming to expand his territory. His campaign faces resistance from Byzantine forces, highlighting the ongoing conflicts in the region.
events.name: Malik Shah begins incursions into Anatolia

events.enhanced_description: Seljuk forces under Toghtekin intervene in the siege of Tyre, compelling King Baldwin I of Jerusalem to abandon his efforts. This intervention underscores the complex military dynamics of the Crusades.
events.name: Seljuk forces intervene at Tyre

events.enhanced_description: The Crusaders undertake a challenging journey to return to Acre, facing numerous obstacles along the way. This event highlights the ongoing struggles and resilience of the Crusader forces in the Holy Land.
events.name: The Crusaders fight their way back to Acre

events.enhanced_description: Henry, the count of Portugal, succumbs to wounds sustained during a siege at Astorga, leading to a power transition as his young son Afonso I becomes his successor. This event marks a significant moment in the early history of Portugal.
events.name: Henry, count of Portugal, dies from wounds received during a siege

events.enhanced_description: In 1113, the Republic of Florence successfully conquered the neighboring city of Montecascioli, a strategic move in its efforts to expand control over the surrounding provinces of Italy. This conquest contributed to Florence's growing influence in the region.
events.name: The Republic of Florence conquers Montecascioli

events.enhanced_description: Around 1113, Peter Abelard, a prominent French philosopher, established his school in Paris, which became a center for scholastic thought and education. His teachings significantly influenced medieval philosophy and the development of the university system in Europe.
events.name: Peter Abelard opens his school in Paris

events.enhanced_description: In 1113, Queen Urraca of Castile made an unsuccessful attempt to reclaim the city of Burgos from her ex-husband, King Alfonso I of Aragon. This conflict exemplified the turbulent political dynamics and personal rivalries of the time.
events.name: Queen Urraca of Castile attempts to seize Burgos

events.enhanced_description: In 1113, the Chinese painter Wang Ximeng completed 'A Thousand Li of Rivers and Mountains,' a monumental landscape painting that remains a hallmark of Song dynasty art. This work is celebrated for its intricate detail and representation of the natural world.
events.name: A Thousand Li of Rivers and Mountains is finished

events.enhanced_description: In 1113, Suryavarman II ascended to the throne of the Khmer Empire, initiating a reign that would see significant architectural and cultural achievements, including the construction of Angkor Wat. His leadership marked a golden age for the Khmer civilization.
events.name: King Suryavarman II begins his reign

events.enhanced_description: Around 1113, Bridlington Priory was established in England, within the Diocese of York. This foundation contributed to the spread of monasticism and religious life in medieval England.
events.name: Bridlington Priory is founded

events.enhanced_description: On January 15, 1113, the Knights Hospitaller, an order established to protect pilgrims in the Holy Land, received formal recognition through the papal bull issued by Pope Paschal II. This recognition solidified the order's role in the Crusades and its commitment to humanitarian efforts.
events.name: The Order of Knights of the Hospital of Saint John of Jerusalem is formally recognized

events.enhanced_description: In the spring of 1113, Malik Shah, the Seljuk ruler, launched an expedition against Nicaea, leading to significant military engagements in the region. Emperor Alexios I Komnenos intervened, ultimately lifting the siege and achieving a decisive victory near Cotyaeum, which showcased the ongoing conflicts between the Byzantine Empire and the Seljuks.
events.name: Spring – Siege of Nicaea

events.enhanced_description: On April 16, 1113, Sviatopolk II, Grand Prince of Kiev, passed away after a two-decade reign, leading to the ascension of his cousin Vladimir II Monomakh. Vladimir's leadership marked a pivotal moment as he initiated campaigns against the Cumans to unify the fragmented territories of Kievan Rus'.
events.name: Sviatopolk II, Grand Prince of Kiev, dies

events.enhanced_description: On June 28, 1113, the Crusaders, led by Baldwin I, faced a significant defeat at the Battle of Al-Sannabra against the Seljuk forces commanded by Mawdud ibn Altuntash. This battle highlighted the ongoing conflict between Crusader states and Muslim powers in the region, with Mawdud's forces conducting raids that further destabilized the area.
events.name: Battle of Al-Sannabra

events.enhanced_description: In September 1113, King Baldwin I of Jerusalem married Adelaide del Vasto, a union that was politically significant but controversial due to Baldwin's existing marriage. This marriage aimed to strengthen alliances in the region amidst the complex political landscape of the Crusader states.
events.name: King Baldwin I of Jerusalem marries Adelaide del Vasto

events.enhanced_description: On September 7, 1113, the Republic of Pisa formalized a treaty with Ramon Berenguer III, Count of Barcelona, initiating a campaign against the Moors in the Balearic Islands. This alliance was crucial for the Pisan fleet's military endeavors in the Mediterranean.
events.name: The Republic of Pisa signs a treaty with Ramon Berenguer III

events.enhanced_description: In 1114, Count Ramon Berenguer III of Barcelona participated in a military expedition to the Balearic Islands, where a combined Pisan and Catalan fleet successfully conquered Ibiza and Mallorca. This campaign was crucial for eliminating Moorish pirate bases in the Mediterranean.
events.name: Count Ramon Berenguer III joins the expedition to the Balearic Islands

events.enhanced_description: In 1114, the Battle of Martorell took place, where the Almoravid governor of Zaragoza, Muhàmmad ibn al-Hajj, launched an offensive against the County of Barcelona but was decisively defeated by Ramon Berenguer III. This battle underscored the ongoing military conflicts in the region during the Reconquista.
events.name: Battle of Martorell

events.enhanced_description: In 1114, Count Routrou II aligned himself with King Alfonso I of Aragon, reflecting the Norman expansion into the Iberian Peninsula. This alliance was part of the broader context of territorial struggles and power shifts in medieval Spain.
events.name: Count Routrou II enters the service of King Alfonso I

events.enhanced_description: In 1114, Emperor Hui Zong of the Song dynasty sent a gift of Chinese musical instruments to the Korean court of Goryeo at the request of King Yejong. This gesture exemplified the cultural exchanges between China and Korea during this period.
events.name: Emperor Hui Zong sends musical instruments to Korea

events.enhanced_description: In 1114, the wooden cathedral of Chichester was tragically destroyed by fire, leading to significant loss of religious and cultural heritage. This event prompted discussions about the construction of more durable structures in the future.
events.name: The cathedral of Chichester is destroyed by fire

events.enhanced_description: Around 1114, Pontigny Abbey, a Cistercian monastery, was founded in Burgundy, France. This establishment contributed to the spread of the Cistercian order and its emphasis on asceticism and community life.
events.name: Pontigny Abbey is founded

events.enhanced_description: On January 7, 1114, Emperor Henry V married Matilda, the young daughter of King Henry I of England, in Worms. This politically motivated union aimed to strengthen ties between the Holy Roman Empire and England but led to significant political strife within the empire shortly thereafter.
events.name: Emperor Henry V marries Matilda

events.enhanced_description: On November 29, 1114, a significant earthquake struck the regions occupied by Crusaders in the Middle East, causing extensive damage from Antioch to Edessa. This natural disaster had profound implications for the stability and security of Crusader territories.
events.name: A large earthquake damages Crusader areas in the Middle East

events.enhanced_description: In 1115, King Baldwin I of Jerusalem commissioned the construction of the Crusader castle of Montreal during a military expedition against the Seljuk Turks. This fortification served as a strategic stronghold in the ongoing conflicts in the region.
events.name: The Crusader castle of Montreal is commissioned

events.enhanced_description: The Jin Dynasty, established by the Jurchen chieftain Taizu (Aguda), represents a pivotal moment in Chinese history as it introduced a dual-administration system combining Jurchen and Chinese bureaucratic practices. This marked the beginning of significant Jurchen influence over northern China.
events.name: Creation of the Jin Dynasty

events.enhanced_description: Minamoto no Tameyoshi, a notable samurai and nobleman, earns recognition for his role in suppressing a riot against Emperor Toba at a monastery near Kyoto. This event highlights the ongoing power struggles and the role of samurai in the political landscape of Japan.
events.name: Minamoto no Tameyoshi gains recognition

events.enhanced_description: In a significant battle, the Mixtec ruler Eight Deer Jaguar Claw is defeated and sacrificed by a coalition of city-states led by his brother-in-law, 4 Wind, at Tilantongo. This event underscores the complex political and military dynamics among the Mixtec city-states.
events.name: Defeat of Eight Deer Jaguar Claw

events.enhanced_description: Arnulf of Chocques, the patriarch of Jerusalem, faces accusations of engaging in sexual relations with a Muslim woman, leading to his temporary removal from office. This incident reflects the tensions and complexities of religious and political authority in the Crusader states.
events.name: Accusation against Arnulf of Chocques

events.enhanced_description: Peter Abelard, a prominent French philosopher, takes on the role of master at the cathedral school of Notre-Dame, where he meets Héloïse d'Argenteuil. Their relationship becomes one of the most famous love stories of the Middle Ages, intertwining themes of love, philosophy, and tragedy.
events.name: Peter Abelard becomes master of Notre-Dame

events.enhanced_description: Clairvaux Abbey is founded by Bernard of Clairvaux, a key figure in the reform of Benedictine monasticism. This establishment becomes a center for spiritual renewal and the Cistercian movement, influencing monastic life across Europe.
events.name: Foundation of Clairvaux Abbey

events.enhanced_description: Hugh of Saint Victor, a notable theologian and writer, joins the Victorines at the Augustinian Abbey of St. Victor in Paris. His contributions to theology and education significantly impact medieval scholastic thought.
events.name: Hugh of Saint Victor joins the Victorines

events.enhanced_description: Al-Khāzini wrote astronomical tables under Sultan Sanjar’s patronage. The text dates the tables to 1115.

image.caption: A manuscript page showing al-Khazini’s Sanjar astronomical tables.
image.date_qualification: A later manuscript witness to the tables, not a contemporary image of their composition. The saved image date is 1919.
image.rights_statement: LicenseShortName: Public domain; UsageTerms: Public domain; Copyrighted: False

events.name: Al-Khāzini’s astronomical tables for Sultan Sanjar

events.enhanced_description: The Battle of Welfesholz marks a significant conflict in the struggle between the German monarchy and the rebellious Saxon nobility. Duke Lothair of Supplinburg allied with the Saxons to defeat the forces of Emperor Henry V, showcasing the ongoing tensions within the Holy Roman Empire.
events.name: Battle of Welfesholz

events.enhanced_description: Matilda of Tuscany, a powerful feudal lord and supporter of the papacy, dies in Bondeno. Her reign was marked by her fierce opposition to Emperor Henry IV, particularly over inheritance rights in Lombardy and Tuscany, which significantly influenced the political landscape of Italy.
events.name: Death of Matilda, Margravine of Tuscany

events.enhanced_description: On September 14, 1115, the Crusaders, led by Prince Roger of Salerno, achieved a surprising victory against the Seljuk Turkish army at the Battle of Sarmin. This battle was significant for the Crusaders as it allowed them to consolidate their control around Antioch.
events.name: Battle of Sarmin

events.enhanced_description: Ramon Berenguer III, Count of Barcelona, travels to Rome to seek support for his crusade against the Moors in Spain. His efforts to gain papal endorsement reflect the intertwining of religious and military objectives during the period.
events.name: Ramon Berenguer III sails to Rome

events.enhanced_description: Countess Theresa of Portugal leads forces to capture the Galician cities of Tui and Ourense, prompting a military response from her sister, Queen Urraca of León and Castile. This conflict illustrates the familial and political rivalries of the time.
events.name: Portuguese forces capture Galician cities

events.enhanced_description: Almoravid troops successfully conquer the Balearic Islands, capitalizing on the weakened state of the local Moorish rulers due to previous raids. This conquest highlights the shifting power dynamics in the Mediterranean during the early 12th century.
events.name: Almoravid conquest of the Balearic Islands

events.enhanced_description: King Gruffydd ap Rhys of Deheubarth leads an attack on Llandovery Castle, which ends in defeat. His subsequent assault on Swansea Castle demonstrates the ongoing conflicts between Welsh princes and the Anglo-Norman lords.
events.name: Welsh attack on Llandovery Castle

events.enhanced_description: Ali ibn Yahya, the Zirid ruler of Ifriqiya, conquers the island of Jerba, which had been functioning as an independent piratical republic. This conquest signifies the consolidation of Zirid power in the region.
events.name: Conquest of Jerba by Ali ibn Yahya

events.enhanced_description: Aak music is introduced to the Korean court through a significant gift from Emperor Hui Zong of the Song dynasty, which includes 428 musical instruments and 572 costumes. This cultural exchange enriches the musical traditions of Korea.
events.name: Introduction of Aak music to Korea

events.enhanced_description: Construction begins on the Chennakeshava Temple at Belur, commissioned by King Vishnuvardhana. This temple becomes a significant example of Hoysala architecture and a center for worship in southern India.
events.name: Construction of Chennakeshava Temple

events.enhanced_description: The monastery at Peterborough in England is destroyed by fire, marking a significant loss for the local community and the monastic tradition. This event reflects the vulnerabilities of religious institutions during this period.
events.name: Destruction of Peterborough Monastery

events.enhanced_description: King Coloman of Hungary passes away after a 21-year reign characterized by the consolidation of the feudal system and territorial expansion, including the overthrow of King Peter II of Croatia. His death marks a pivotal transition in Hungarian leadership.
events.name: Death of King Coloman of Hungary

events.enhanced_description: During the summer, Crusaders led by King Baldwin I of Jerusalem embark on an expedition to Egypt, reaching Akaba on the Red Sea. They establish fortifications to secure control over vital caravan routes, furthering Crusader interests in the region.
events.name: Crusaders expedition to Egypt

events.enhanced_description: Doge Ordelafo Faliero of Venice achieves victory over Hungarian forces led by King Stephen II, leading to the surrender of remaining Dalmatian towns to Venice. This battle underscores the ongoing territorial conflicts in the Adriatic region.
events.name: Defeat of Hungarian troops by Venice

events.enhanced_description: In the Battle of Philomelion, Emperor Alexios I Komnenos leads a Byzantine expedition against the Seljuk Turks under Sultan Malik Shah. The Byzantines employ a new defensive formation, successfully repelling multiple attacks and claiming victory, which reinforces Byzantine control in Anatolia.
events.name: Battle of Philomelion

events.enhanced_description: In the autumn, King Baldwin I of Jerusalem initiates the construction of Scandelion Castle at the Ladder of Tyre, effectively blockading the city from the mainland. This strategic move is part of Baldwin's efforts to consolidate Crusader control in the region.
events.name: Construction of Scandelion Castle

events.enhanced_description: King Stephen II of Hungary successfully regains control of Dalmatia from Venice while the Venetians are occupied elsewhere. This victory is significant in the ongoing territorial disputes in the Adriatic region.
events.name: Regaining of Dalmatia by King Stephen II

events.enhanced_description: Ramon Berenguer III, Count of Barcelona, inherits Cerdanya, a region located between the Pyrenees and the Ebro River. This inheritance strengthens the Principality of Catalonia and enhances Berenguer's political power.
events.name: Inheritance of Cerdanya by Ramon Berenguer III

events.enhanced_description: Vladislaus I abdicates in favor of his brother Bořivoj II, yet retains significant power behind the scenes. This transition reflects the complexities of power dynamics within the Bohemian nobility.
events.name: Abdication of Vladislaus I of Bohemia

events.enhanced_description: In 1117, the Almoravid dynasty briefly regained control of Coimbra, a significant city in modern Portugal, during the ongoing conflicts in the Iberian Peninsula. This reconquest reflects the shifting power dynamics between Muslim and Christian states in the region during the Reconquista.
events.name: The Almoravids briefly reconquer Coimbra (modern Portugal)

events.enhanced_description: In 1148, the Battle of Ghazni saw Ghurid forces under Sayf al-Din Suri decisively defeat the Ghaznavid Sultan Bahram-Shah, leading to the capture of the capital Ghazni. This victory not only marked a significant territorial shift but also showcased the rising power of the Ghurids in the region.
events.name: Battle of Ghazni

events.enhanced_description: In 1117, a conflict erupted between the independent Muslim republics of Gabès and Mahdia in modern Tunisia, with Mahdia receiving support from the Zirid Dynasty and Gabès aided by Roger II of Sicily. This conflict highlights the regional power struggles in Ifriqiya during this period.
events.name: Conflict between Gabès and Mahdia

events.enhanced_description: In 1117, the Crusaders, led by King Baldwin I of Jerusalem, launched a raid on Pelusium in Egypt, resulting in the city's destruction. Following this raid, Baldwin fortified the southern frontiers of his kingdom, reflecting the ongoing military campaigns of the Crusades.
events.name: Crusaders raid Pelusium

events.enhanced_description: In 1117, King Mahaabarana Adeettiya, also known as Koimala, became the first king to unify the Maldives, reclaiming the northern atolls from Indian invaders. His reign marked a significant moment in the history of the Maldives, establishing a centralized authority.
events.name: King Mahaabarana Adeettiya (Koimala) becomes king of the Maldives

events.enhanced_description: In 1117, the warrior monks known as sōhei from Mii-dera and Enryaku-ji united their forces to attack the city of Nara in Japan. This conflict illustrates the growing power of religious warriors in Japanese society during this period.
events.name: Sōhei attack Nara

events.enhanced_description: In 1117, Merton Priory, located near London, was consecrated, becoming a significant center for learning and diplomacy in England. The priory played a crucial role in the religious and cultural life of the region during the medieval period.
events.name: Merton Priory consecrated

events.enhanced_description: In 1117, the magnetic compass was first utilized for maritime navigation during the Song Dynasty in China. This innovation greatly enhanced navigation at sea, facilitating exploration and trade across vast distances.
events.name: First use of magnetic compass

events.enhanced_description: The 1117 Verona earthquake struck northern Italy and parts of Germany, causing significant destruction, particularly in Verona where the outer wall of the amphitheater was severely damaged. This event led to a major reconstruction effort, transforming the architectural landscape of the city.
events.name: 1117 Verona earthquake

events.enhanced_description: In 1118, a peace agreement was reached between England and Flanders, marking a significant diplomatic achievement in the context of ongoing conflicts in Europe. This agreement helped stabilize relations and foster trade between the two regions.
events.name: Peace between England and Flanders

events.enhanced_description: In 1118, Enna mac Donnchada mac Murchada ascended to the throne as King of Dublin, a pivotal moment in the city's history. His reign contributed to the consolidation of power in the region during a time of political fragmentation.
events.name: Enna mac Donnchada mac Murchada becomes King of Dublin

events.enhanced_description: In 1118, Cu Faifne mac Congalaig was proclaimed King of Uí Failghe, a significant event in the local governance of Ireland. His leadership would play a role in the shifting allegiances and power structures of the time.
events.name: Cu Faifne mac Congalaig becomes King of Uí Failghe

events.enhanced_description: In 1118, Maelsechlainn Ua Faelain became the King of Déisi Muman, marking an important development in the regional leadership of Ireland. His reign would influence the local dynamics of power and governance.
events.name: Maelsechlainn Ua Faelain becomes King of Déisi Muman

events.enhanced_description: In 1118, Gruffudd ap Cynan, King of Gwynedd, successfully annexed the cantrefs of Rhos and Rhufoniog, strengthening his rule in Wales. This expansion reflects the ongoing struggles for power among Welsh leaders during this period.
events.name: Gruffudd ap Cynan annexes Rhos and Rhufoniog

events.enhanced_description: In 1118, a significant change occurred in ecclesiastical protocol as the Archbishop of York was no longer required to be crowned by the Archbishop of Canterbury. This shift indicated a growing assertion of independence within the English church hierarchy.
events.name: Archbishop of York's coronation change

events.enhanced_description: In 1118, reconstruction began on Peterborough Cathedral, which had been destroyed by fire in 1116. This rebuilding effort was significant for the architectural and cultural heritage of England, symbolizing resilience and continuity.
events.name: Reconstruction of Peterborough Cathedral

events.enhanced_description: In 1118, Đorđe, the Vojislavljević ruler of Serbia, was overthrown by Uroš I of Raška, marking a significant political shift in the region. This event reflects the turbulent nature of Serbian politics during the early 12th century.
events.name: Overthrow of Đorđe, Vojislavljević ruler of Serbia

events.enhanced_description: In 1118, George I of Duklja was overthrown by his cousin Grubeša, a significant event in the political landscape of the region. This power struggle illustrates the complexities of dynastic politics in medieval Montenegro.
events.name: Overthrow of George I of Duklja
